header:
Date: 2026-02-03
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Vargas (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (SageBank), Evan Brooks (SageBank), Priya Singh (SageBank), Tommy Lee (SageBank)
summary: Kickoff POC scoping to define success criteria for a banking chatbot pilot. Focus areas: traffic characterization (QPS, concurrency), token distribution, latency SLO, cost targets, and benchmark design. Agreed next steps: share benchmark harness, customer to provide traffic telemetry and prompt set. Plan for a benchmark window by end of week and follow-up in 7 days.
topics: Input/output token distribution and prompt ensembles
Benchmark design: synthetic vs replay, duration
Security/compliance notes (data residency, KMS, audit logs)
Timeline and success criteria for pilot
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Diego from our SE team is with me. Can you all hear me okay?
00:06 Anita Rao: Yep, loud and clear.
00:08 Diego Vargas: Hi folks. Quick agenda — characterize your peak QPS and token mix, agree success criteria, and plan benchmark window.
00:15 Tommy Lee: Sounds good. We want to make sure the pilot reflects real banking traffic not some toy chatty prompts.
00:20 Maya Chen: Absolutely. Anita, could you start with current usage shape — QPS, concurrency, any burst patterns you see?
00:27 Anita Rao: Sure. So our current user facing assistant is fairly new. Average QPS is low — like 3 to 6 qps during business hours — but we get these spikes around 12:30 and 16:00 where it jumps to 40 to 60 for a few minutes, like payroll windows. We also have nightly batch ingestion where internal jobs call the model for enrichment — that's bursty but lower priority.
00:48 Evan Brooks: To add, the concurrency visible at runtime — at peak we see about 20 concurrent sessions, p95 token latencies currently with our self-hosted model are around 700ms but that's including some CPU-bound tails.
00:59 Maya Chen: Ok that burst profile is helpful. One common pattern we see is a low steady baseline with heavy episodic spikes. For POC benchmarking we'll want to model both steady-state and the short spikes — otherwise sizing will be off.
01:12 Diego Vargas: Quick clarifier: when you say token latency 700ms, is that end-to-end server response time or just inference?
01:18 Evan Brooks: That's full stack, includes network and pre/post processing. Pure inference is closer to 250–300ms on average for our quantized model.
01:27 Priya Singh: From a security perspective, we need to validate KMS integration and audit logs. Also data residency requirements — PII can’t leave EU regions for certain customers though SageBank's pilot is US-only for now.
01:38 Maya Chen: Noted. Redwood's private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we'll include our SOC2 artifacts in the package we send.
01:45 Tommy Lee: Great. Back to workload — do you have a sample prompt set or token distribution? Short banking prompts vs long document summarization will change tokens a lot.
01:55 Anita Rao: We do. We'll export a small ensemble: 70% short prompts (~20–60 input tokens, 40–80 output tokens), 20% medium (~150 input, 100–300 output), 10% long (docs, ~600+ input, 500+ output). The long ones are mostly internal jobs and can be scheduled.
02:14 Diego Vargas: Perfect — that's the distribution we need. For throttling and batching we'll treat the long ones as lower priority in the benchmark so they don't skew latency SLOs for interactive users.
02:24 Maya Chen: Let's capture success criteria. Typical banks want p95 < 250ms and p99 < 600ms for interactive flows. Is that reasonable for you, or too aggressive?
02:34 Anita Rao: p95 250 is ambitious given our current infra, but if Redwood can show consistent p95 <= 300 and p99 <= 700 under the mixed workload that would be a win. Cost target: we can't exceed our current per-call spend by more than 40% during the pilot.
02:47 Maya Chen: Ok p95 <= 300 and p99 <= 700 and cost delta <= +40% — noted. We'll design benchmarks to report latency and cost per 1k tokens.
02:58 Evan Brooks: Also need a target conversational context length. We typically keep context to last 6 turns, average conversation output tokens around 60.
03:06 Diego Vargas: Thanks. For sizing I'll propose two configurations: a small dedicated pool tuned for low-latency interactive requests and a cheaper scaleout config for batch/long-form. We'll bench both.
03:18 Tommy Lee: How long will the benchmark runs be? We need to know how to carve out a window.
03:22 Maya Chen: For steady-state we usually run 30–60 minutes at representative QPS. For burst stress we'll do a 10–15 minute spike at peak QPS. For end-to-end we recommend a 2–3 hour run if you want a full picture, but for the POC initial pass 90 minutes is sufficient.
03:41 Anita Rao: 90 minutes works. We'll provide production telemetry for the last week so you can generate a replay too.
03:47 Diego Vargas: Replay is great. Replay gives us realistic request mixes, but we'll also run synthetic scenarios to isolate variables — e.g., strip network overhead to measure pure inference kernel p50/p95/p99.
03:58 Priya Singh: On compliance, we need to confirm log retention and role-based access. Can Redwood's console restrict redwood staff access to telemetry?
04:07 Maya Chen: Yes, in Dedicated and Private modes we support RBAC and audit logs. We'll include the config options and a short runbook for least-privilege.
04:16 Anita Rao: Any thought on quantization — we saw some quality regression with 4-bit in another test. We care more about answer correctness than micro-cost savings.
04:25 Diego Vargas: Understood. We'll include quantization profiles. For the POC we'll test two weight formats: 8-bit commercially safe and a tuned 4-bit option. We'll run quality regressions using your prompt set and measure rouge/embedding-similarity checks.
04:39 Tommy Lee: How do you measure quality automatically? We don't want manual review for every run.
04:44 Diego Vargas: We use a combination: reference answers for deterministic prompts, embedding cosine similarity for open-ended replies, and token-level hallucination metrics for factual prompts. We'll produce a report per run.
04:56 Maya Chen: Let's define concrete KPIs for the pilot: 1) p95/p99 latency under mixed workload, 2) cost per 1k tokens and delta vs your baseline, 3) model quality pass rate > 95% on our eval set, 4) successful KMS/audit integration. Sound right?
05:11 Anita Rao: Yes. Also uptime during the run must be >= 99.9%.
05:16 Maya Chen: We'll aim to meet that SLA for Dedicated pilot.
05:19 Evan Brooks: About network topology — we'll run benchmarks from our VPC in us-east-1. Does Redwood have a peering option?
05:26 Diego Vargas: We offer VPC peering and Private (on-prem) connectors. For the POC, peering to our Dedicated cluster in us-east-1 is straightforward; we'll share the subnet and firewall requirements.
05:36 Priya Singh: Please include the least-privilege firewall/IP list. We cannot open wide ranges.
05:40 Maya Chen: We'll provide exact CIDR ranges.
05:43 Tommy Lee: Who will run the benchmark? Your team or ours?
05:46 Diego Vargas: We can run it on our side if you provide the telemetry and an encoded prompt set. Alternatively, we can share the harness and you run it inside your environment and push results back. Both have pros — us-running is faster but customer-run gives more fidelity.
05:59 Anita Rao: Let's have Redwood run the first benchmark to get baseline, then we'll run a replay in-house for parity.
06:04 Maya Chen: Good plan. We'll need your sample prompt set, a 7-day QPS trace, and any filters for PII.
06:12 Evan Brooks: We'll scrub PII and deliver. Expect 1.5MB of logs zipped.
06:16 Diego Vargas: For the sizing recommendation, can you confirm expected sustained QPS for pilot? You mentioned spikes to 60 qps — what baseline should we assume for the sustained phase?
06:26 Anita Rao: Baseline 5 qps but for the pilot steady-state we want to test 8 qps sustained, with two spike scenarios: a short 60 qps spike and a moderate 25 qps spike for 10 minutes.
06:36 Diego Vargas: Great. We'll model that: steady 8 qps for 45 minutes, then a 10-min 60 qps stress, then a 15-min 25 qps medium burst. We'll surface p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization.
06:49 Maya Chen: Any internal constraints on go-live timeline? Tommy?
06:53 Tommy Lee: We want a decision in 6 weeks, pilot running in 2–3 weeks if all goes smooth. So POC needs to deliver benchmark results and a recommended sizing within that window.
07:03 Maya Chen: We can meet that: benchmarking this week, follow-up next week, and pilot provisioning in week three.
07:09 Priya Singh: On the legal side, we need a minimal DPA and SOC2 report before pilot starts. Also a short statement on encryption in transit and at rest.
07:18 Maya Chen: We'll attach our standard DPA and SOC2 summary. Redwood's Dedicated supports customer KMS and TLS 1.3 in transit; we'll include exact cipher suites in the attachment.
07:27 Diego Vargas: Small technical note — for replaying production traffic we sometimes need to normalize timestamps and session IDs to avoid caches blowing up. If you can remove identifiable session tokens, that helps.
07:38 Evan Brooks: We'll anonymize session IDs and replace PII.
07:41 Anita Rao: For quality checks, can you surface example failure cases? We want to be able to triage quickly.
07:47 Diego Vargas: Absolutely; each run will include a triage summary with the top N failures, sample traces, and input/output token counts.
07:54 Tommy Lee: Ok. Are there any architectural red flags we should be aware of?
07:59 Diego Vargas: One common surprise is KV cache sizing for long context models. If you push a lot of long-form jobs, you'll need to plan KV memory. From what you said, long jobs are low priority, so we can route them to a different pool to avoid polluting the interactive cache.
08:13 Anita Rao: Good call. Also what about cost accounting? We need token-level billing aligned to product metrics.
08:19 Maya Chen: Redwood console provides token-level breakdown by route/model and per-token cost. We'll share a screenshot in the follow up.
08:26 Priya Singh: Anything about model versions? We need version pinning to avoid drift during pilot.
08:31 Diego Vargas: Yes, you can pin model versions and roll out with canaries. We'll include a rollout policy.
08:37 Maya Chen: Let's recap next steps and owners.
08:40 Maya Chen: Action items — (1) Maya to send benchmark harness and runbook; (2) Evan to provide telemetry and anonymized logs; (3) Anita to share prompt set and quality targets; (4) Diego to propose sizing and quant profiles. We'll schedule a follow-up in 7 days.
08:56 Tommy Lee: That matches my notes. Thanks everyone.
08:59 Maya Chen: Thank you. We'll email the packet and proposed benchmark window by EOD tomorrow.
09:04 Anita Rao: Appreciate it. Looking forward.
09:07 Diego Vargas: Thanks all. Bye.
